summary.text: 比 means “compare” or “match.” Its early Shang use is read variously as “follow,” “ally,” or “assist,” and its precise sense remains disputed.

formation.text: 比’s early construction is disputed. One analysis treats it as two person-like figures placed side by side; another proposes two 匕 signs, each picturing a shallow, long-handled food ladle, whose juxtaposition suggests nearness. That account also assigns 匕 a sound-cue role, but reconstructed similarity alone does not establish the role or the signs’ identity. The Han dictionary instead explains 比 as two 人 forms reversed from 从.

components.text: The person-like analysis treats the two figures as people placed side by side, suggesting juxtaposition; the early signs’ identity remains disputed.

In this disputed analysis, each 匕 is a picture of a shallow, long-handled food ladle; placing two together suggests nearness. The account separately proposes 匕 as a sound cue, though the reconstructed resemblance does not establish that role or the signs’ identity.

sound_limitation.text: The reconstructed sound resemblance does not establish that 匕 is a component of 比, or identify the referent of the early signs.

sound.text: In the Baxter–Sagart system, 匕 and 比 have similar Old Chinese reconstructions; this comparison alone does not prove a phonetic role.
Both characters have the modern Mandarin reading bǐ; this current match does not establish an ancient sound relationship.

components.text: The Han dictionary analyzes 比 as two 人 forms reversed from 从. This historical account is not confirmed by the cited early-script analyses.

history.text: A character study records several Shang forms and later graphic variation while noting continuity in the graph’s basic structure. These changes do not by themselves establish what the graph depicts.

The Han dictionary explains 比 as two 人 forms reversed from 从. Other accounts describe person-like figures or propose two 匕 forms; these competing identities and analyses do not settle the early graph’s construction.

uncertainties.text: The early graph’s referent and any role for 匕 remain unsettled. A 1948 study’s argument could not be checked, and the cited early forms have not been individually verified.
The relationship between the Shang use and later senses is unclear: the early phrase has competing readings, while classical examples do not establish a dated sequence of meanings.

senses.text: In the early Shang phrase 王比望乘, 比 has been read as “follow” or “lead,” “form a close alliance,” or “assist” and “support.” Its precise sense is disputed.

senses.gloss: associate with; attach to a group or person
senses.text: A classical passage is conventionally understood as referring to partial association or factional attachment. Association and following uses are also recorded, but their chronology is unresolved.
比 is used to compare or match. A poem uses it of matching a team of horses, but this example does not date the sense’s beginning or show how it relates to other meanings.
A Zhouyi commentary glosses 比 as “assist” or “support.” This resembles one proposed reading of the Shang phrase, whose meaning remains disputed.
A reconstruction table distinguishes a reading glossed “combine; all” from the reading glossed “compare,” but does not establish how the uses relate or when they arose.

developments.text: Some interpretations connect the Shang use with later association, but the early phrase is disputed, so this development is unresolved.
“Assist” or “support” is one reading of the Shang phrase, but other interpretations differ; a development into the later gloss cannot be established.

limitations.text: Dictionary glosses and classical examples do not establish a chronological sequence among the senses. The dates of the specific written witnesses remain unresolved.

overview.text: 比 means ‘compare’ or ‘match’ today. In its standard form, the left side has a short horizontal stroke and a rising vertical stroke; the right has a short horizontal stroke and a curved-hook vertical stroke.
